name: ss
summary: Shows sockets: connections and listening ports.
description: Socket statistics: the modern, faster replacement for netstat. It lists network connections (TCP, UDP) and local sockets. The classic reflex to find out which program is listening on which port: sudo ss -tulpn. You can also filter by state or port right in the command.

options.description: Ports and addresses as numbers (22 instead of ssh).
Shows the program using each socket (sudo to see everything).

arguments.name: FILTER
arguments.description: Optional filter: state established, sport = :443, dst 192.168.1.10…

examples.explanation: Listening TCP and UDP ports, as numbers, with the program behind each.
examples.output:
Netid State  Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port Peer Address:Port Process
tcp   LISTEN 0      128          0.0.0.0:22        0.0.0.0:*     users:(("sshd",pid=812,fd=3))

examples.explanation: Checks that something is listening on the PostgreSQL port.
